questions.title: Prostatic carcinoma produces osteosclerotic bone metastases
questions.question: Which one of these tumours metastasizing in bone is osteosclerotic:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Breast carcinoma's bone metastases are classically mixed (both lytic and sclerotic), not the purely osteosclerotic pattern this question asks for.
explanations.B: Correct. Prostatic carcinoma characteristically produces osteosclerotic (osteoblastic) bone metastases, in which new bone formation dominates over resorption, giving a dense, radio-opaque appearance on imaging. This is a distinctive teaching point that helps distinguish prostatic metastases from the classically osteolytic pattern of renal cell carcinoma and thyroid carcinoma, and from bronchogenic carcinoma's typically lytic metastases.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Renal cell carcinoma's bone metastases are classically osteolytic, the opposite pattern from the osteosclerotic one this question asks for.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Bronchogenic (lung) carcinoma's bone metastases are typically osteolytic, not osteosclerotic.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Thyroid carcinoma's bone metastases are classically osteolytic, not osteosclerotic.
